chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from some of his men from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever is obliged to offer a sacrificial animal (hady) while in ihram, he may slaughter it wherever he wishes.
Except for the compensation for game (fidyah), for indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: 'A sacrifice reaching the Ka'ba.'

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And everything whose origin is in the 'Sea' (Al-Jawad), the issue is the origin. And its mention has passed. Then he said (may Allah have mercy on him): And there is no harm for the Muhrim to eat what the Muhrim hunted, and the compensation is upon the Muhrim.

key_terms.الْمُحِلُّ: The one who is not in the state of ihram (or the one exempted)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of ihram
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: Sacrificial animal offered by a pilgrim

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim slaughter their sacrificial animal during ihram, and what is the exception for game compensation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the jurisprudential principle that the specific Quranic command 'a sacrifice reaching the Ka'ba' (2:196) applies strictly to the compensation for hunting game (fidya), whereas other obligatory sacrifices (hady) may be slaughtered anywhere. This distinction clarifies the flexibility in ritual slaughter locations while maintaining the sanctity of the Ka'ba for specific expiations, reflecting the Usuli approach to deriving legal rulings from textual evidence.
